en.headline: Police receive 1,209 reports of unauthorised iPhone pre-orders worth HK$25 million
en.dek: The figure has risen from more than 700 reports and HK$14.7 million disclosed a day earlier; orders have not been shipped and banks and Apple are cancelling transactions.
body: Hong Kong police said on Monday evening that they had received 1,209 reports of unauthorised credit-card transactions linked to pre-orders of the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, with a total sum of about HK$25 million.

Superintendent Cheung Hau-yee of the Technology Crime Division said the cases were provisionally classified as obtaining property by deception. Police had passed details to the banks and Apple so that affected transactions could be cancelled before any phones were shipped.

Initial inquiries found no evidence of a network attack on Apple’s or the banks’ systems. Many of the online pre-order payments did not require a one-time password or other holder confirmation, which investigators said may have made the fraud easier. Police are examining how the card data were obtained and are tracing the digital footprints of those who placed the orders.

zh.headline: 警方接獲1209人報案疑盜卡預購iPhone 涉款約2500萬元
zh.dek: 數字由前晚逾700宗、1470萬元上升；涉案訂單尚未出貨，警方已交銀行及蘋果公司取消交易。
body: 警方周一晚表示，截至當日下午5時，已接獲1209名市民報案，指信用卡在未經授權下被人於蘋果網上商店預購新款iPhone 18 Pro及Pro Max，總涉案金額約2500萬元。
網絡安全及科技罪案調查科科技罪案組警司張巧儀指，案件暫列「以欺騙手段取得財產」。警方已將報案資料交予相關銀行及蘋果公司跟進，以便盡快取消交易，避免損失。據了解，涉案訂單均未出貨。
初步調查顯示銀行及公司系統運作正常，暫不涉網絡攻擊。部分預購交易毋須經單次短訊驗證碼或其他認證即可完成，令持卡人無需確認。警方正追查信用卡資料洩漏源頭，以及實際下單人士的數碼足跡。
